I'll go with this one — the bookmark-shaped button right on the card.

Here's my thinking: "read later" is something I'll flip on and off constantly — that's the whole nature of it, save a pile, then knock items off as I get to them. So for that particular action, one visible click that lights up green feels better than digging into the menu every time. And because it's a toggle that's now showing as "on," the way back is obvious: I just click the same button again to say I'm done with it. That makes the round-trip I was worried about feel completely natural.

To be clear, I still want the menu for the less-frequent stuff like editing — I'm not asking to move everything onto the card. Just this read-later action earns its own visible button because I'll use it so often.

So: the direct button for read-later. Go ahead and add the "finished reading" side of it — and what I'd expect is that clicking that lit-up button again marks it read, drops it out of the Read later list, and ticks the count back down.
